title: CLI joins a name given as several arguments with single spaces
spec: main(argv) in src/samplecli/cli.py uses only the first argument, so `greet Ada Lovelace` (main(['Ada', 'Lovelace'])) prints 'Hello, Ada!' and silently drops the rest. Change main() so the name is built from ALL arguments: join them with spaces, then apply the existing normalisation (greet-003 strip + 'world' fallback, greet-005 collapse of every whitespace run to one ASCII space). ' '.join(' '.join(args).split()) or 'world' is sufficient. Consequences: main(['Ada', 'Lovelace']) prints 'Hello, Ada Lovelace!'; arguments keep their order; whitespace inside or around each argument is collapsed/stripped the same way as for a single argument; blank arguments contribute nothing (main(['Ada', '', '   ', 'Lovelace']) prints 'Hello, Ada Lovelace!'); if every argument is blank, or there are none, the name is 'world'. Single-argument behaviour is unchanged, so tests/test_cli.py, tests/test_cli_blank_name.py and tests/test_cli_collapse_whitespace.py must still pass. main() prints greet(name) and returns 0. Change only src/samplecli/cli.py. greet() in src/samplecli/greet.py must stay byte-for-byte unchanged and must not normalise whitespace. Do not change main()'s signature, add CLI flags or argument-parsing libraries, add public symbols, add dependencies, or edit tests. Risk: no owner_approval category applies — the manifest only lists new_dependency and none is added; main()'s signature, flags and public symbols are unchanged; the change only affects output when more than one argument is given.

criteria.text: main(['Ada', 'Lovelace']) returns 0 and prints exactly 'Hello, Ada Lovelace!\n'
arguments are joined in order: main(['Ada', 'King', 'Lovelace']) prints exactly 'Hello, Ada King Lovelace!\n'
whitespace around and inside joined arguments is stripped and collapsed: main(['  Ada ', '\tKing  ', ' Lovelace\n']) prints exactly 'Hello, Ada King Lovelace!\n'
blank arguments add no extra spaces: main(['Ada', '', '   ', 'Lovelace']) prints exactly 'Hello, Ada Lovelace!\n'
when every argument is blank the name falls back to 'world': main(['', '  ', '\t']) prints exactly 'Hello, world!\n'
a single argument is unchanged: main(['Ada']) prints exactly 'Hello, Ada!\n'
greet() is unchanged and does not normalise whitespace: greet('Ada  Lovelace') == 'Hello, Ada  Lovelace!'

out_of_scope: new CLI flags, public symbols, or argument parsing libraries
changing the greet-003 strip/'world' fallback or greet-005 whitespace-collapse behaviour for a single argument
